item.title: Power restored following North Lynn building fire
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Power restored following North Lynn building fire
Four fire crews were called to a building blaze on Coulton Close in North Lynn yesterday evening. Firefighters from King’s Lynn, Terrington, and Sandringham attended the scene after the alarm was raised at 7:36pm.
To ensure safety during the operation, UK Power Networks isolated electricity supplies to 108 households at 8:29pm. Power was successfully restored to all but one of those properties by 10:05pm. Crews remained on site until the incident was concluded at 1:51am this morning.

item.title: Wisbech carpentry students build play kitchens for local playground
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech carpentry students build play kitchens for local playground
Carpentry students from the College of West Anglia have completed a community project for the Wisbech Adventure Playground. Level 2 students William, Marc, Reece, and Noah designed and built two bespoke play kitchens using reclaimed wood. The finished items were presented to playground representative Violet Loveridge this week.
Course lecturer Jamie Baker said the project allowed students to develop their skills while working sustainably. The new equipment is now available for children to use at The Spinney, with local officials praising the initiative for providing new opportunities for creative play. The project marks a successful collaboration between the college and the local community.

item.title: Series of convictions at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Series of convictions at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
A range of cases were heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court last Thursday. Several individuals appeared before the bench for driving offences, including drink and drug-driving. Among those sentenced were Oliver Saunders of Stoke Ferry, who received a 12-month driving ban for being six times over the cocaine limit, and Kevin Sherman of Necton, who was disqualified for 15 months for drink-driving.
The court also dealt with various theft and public order offences. These included a shoplifting case involving 20 bottles of whisky, a man pleading guilty to cultivating cannabis, and a case involving threatening behaviour at a restaurant in King’s Lynn. Several defendants were issued fines and court costs, with some sentencing hearings adjourned until later this year.

New Ali G film released featuring Sacha Baron Cohen
Sacha Baron Cohen has returned to the screen as his well-known character Ali G in the new film, Ali G: Who Iz I? The movie, which marks Baron Cohen’s directorial debut, follows the character as he travels to America to revive his television career after discovering his girlfriend is expecting a baby.
The production features a mix of scripted scenes alongside the performer's signature hidden-camera encounters with members of the public. While reviews suggest the film’s narrative structure impacts the overall pacing, it continues to include moments of improvisation. The film also stars Morgana Robinson and Stewart Rodeheaver.

item.title: Home Office to proceed with asylum accommodation in Leverington
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Home Office to proceed with asylum accommodation in Leverington
Fenland District Council has expressed deep concern after the Home Office confirmed plans to use Roman Court in Leverington as asylum accommodation. The site is intended to house 26 women and babies. The council had previously raised objections regarding public safety, community cohesion, and the suitability of the location.
The Home Office stated that the site will only become operational once it meets all necessary legal, safety, and regulatory requirements. This decision follows recent public protests and a fire at the property, which remains under police investigation. Officials from the Home Office are scheduled to meet with council and police representatives tomorrow to discuss the matter further.

item.title: Funding secured for new £600,000 fire training facility in South Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Funding secured for new £600,000 fire training facility in South Lynn
A new £600,000 specialist training facility is planned for the South Lynn fire station. The project is being funded through a joint investment of £300,000 each from Norfolk County Council and West Norfolk Council. The facility will be built on vacant land behind the station and is designed to provide realistic training for complex emergencies, including road traffic collisions and rescues at height.
Construction is expected to begin next year, subject to planning consent and site surveys. Currently, crews must travel to North Lynn for essential training. This new development aims to keep firefighters closer to their station, reducing travel time and ensuring crews remain available to respond to emergency calls across West Norfolk.
